role.altitude: The childcare worker keeps observing, caring for and teaching children and talking with parents; paper diaries, attendance lists and searching for activity ideas shrink.
skills_to_grow: Recording observations and daily notes in the parent app as the day goes
role.ambitious_version: A childcare worker with more time on the floor and better notes for parents.

tasks.short: Observe children, note signs of emotional or developmental problems, discuss them with colleagues, bring them to parents' attention and record the conversation.

steps.what: Childcare worker observes children in play and care and identifies signs of emotional or developmental problems
Childcare worker writes observation notes on the child in a notebook
Childcare worker discusses the concern with colleagues and the pedagogical coach
Childcare worker brings the concern to the parents' or guardians' attention in a conversation
Childcare worker records the conversation and agreements in the child's file

tasks.design: Almost nothing changes: noticing a concern, talking it over and telling parents stay with people. Observations are written in a structured form per development area in the centre's childcare system ({OTHER}) instead of a notebook, and the parent conversation is recorded in the same child file with a short template. No model scores or interprets a child's development.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked it; the work is observation and conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Childcare systems hold structured observation forms per child.
tasks.still_hard: Telling parents something they do not want to hear.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a quiet child is not just shy.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the worker's week beyond tidier notes.

reach.task: Support staff on concerns about children
reach.learn: Whether structured observations make referrals clearer.

evidence.claim: Notes on children's health and development are special-category data and must stay in the centre's own system, not a general chatbot.
Scoring a toddler's development with AI might come close to an AI Act high-risk area; the design does not score.

assumptions: Boundary: from observing to the conversation recorded; referral to youth services is outside.
Input contract for s2: an observation form per development area set up in the childcare system by the pedagogical coach; fallback is the notebook.
Observing, discussing and the parent conversation keep their full time.
s2 is the childcare worker's first observation note and keeps its full time; copying notes into the daily record is cut in sibling task 2337.
unknowns: How often concerns are raised per group.
research_questions: Do structured observations change what is raised with parents?

incremental.description: Childcare worker learns the observation form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few concerns and short notes; high: a group with several children needing close observation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct children in eating, toilet and hand-washing habits and rest, and note what each child ate, slept and did for the parents.

steps.what: Childcare worker instructs children in eating habits at meals
Childcare worker helps with toilet habits and hand washing
Childcare worker settles children for rest and sleep
Childcare worker writes what each child ate, slept and did on the toilet in the paper diary for parents

tasks.design: Teaching habits stays hands-on. The only change is the daily note: the worker taps what each child ate, how long they slept and toilet moments on the group tablet in the parent app ({OTHER}) when it happens, and parents see the daily report there instead of in a paper diary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper diaries had to be filled per child at the end of the day.
tasks.enabler_now: Parent apps show a daily report built from staff taps.
tasks.still_hard: Everything that happens with the children.
tasks.human_edge: Patience with a child learning to use the toilet.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes beyond less writing at the end of the day.

reach.learn: Whether parents read the daily report and ask fewer questions at pick-up.

evidence.claim: A Dutch parent app shows parents a timeline, a daily report in a digital diary, photos and the agenda.
The parent app asks parents for diary and photo consent at first login.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: daily care routines and the note for parents; meal planning is outside.
Input contract for s4: the worker's own taps per child on the group tablet as care happens; these are what the child actually ate and slept, not the planned menu or rest times.
Care routines keep their full time; tap time stamps are not used to judge staff.
unknowns: Children per group and whether a tablet is at hand.
research_questions: Do parents ask fewer questions at pick-up?

incremental.description: Childcare worker keeps the group tablet charged and logged in.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an older group with short notes; high: a baby group with detailed feeding and sleep notes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take attendance at arrival and pick-up, have it sent to the office, handle absence and swap-day messages, fill in internal paperwork and make phone calls.

steps.what: Childcare worker takes attendance on a paper list at arrival and pick-up
Office administrator types the paper attendance lists into the childcare system for billing
Parents phone or message about absence and swap days
Childcare worker handles absence messages and swap-day requests and checks group capacity
Childcare worker edits internal paperwork such as incident, allergy and medication forms
Childcare worker makes phone calls to parents about ill children and to colleagues about cover

tasks.design: The worker taps each child in and out on the group tablet in the childcare system ({OTHER}), which records actual arrival and pick-up times and passes them to the office for billing, so nobody types paper lists. Parents report absence and ask for swap days in the parent app with about the effort of a call; the system checks group capacity and the centre's swap rules, and the worker confirms. Incident, allergy and medication forms are filled in the same system; calls about ill children stay by phone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance and requests lived on paper and phone, so the office retyped them.
tasks.enabler_now: Childcare systems take tablet check-ins and parent app requests with capacity rules.
tasks.still_hard: Calls about ill children and finding cover at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a parent who has to leave work for an ill child.
tasks.altitude: Less paper and fewer calls; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether billing from tablet check-ins cuts corrections.

evidence.claim: A Dutch parent app shows parents the agenda and daily reports from the childcare system.
Childcare costs for the benefit run through registered hours and bank payment, not cash.
Tablet time stamps can monitor staff; using them that way needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: daily group admin; invoicing and contracts are the office's work and outside.
Input contract for s2: actual arrival and pick-up times produced by the worker's taps in s1; the system passes them to billing; fallback is the paper list.
Input contract for s4: requests entered by parents in the app (s3), with about the effort of today's call; capacity and swap rules set by the location manager; fallback is the phone.
Coverage: about 80% of parents use the app for requests; s4 is priced at that share.
Calls about ill children keep their full time; office and parent time are outside the worker's savings.
unknowns: Whether the centre's system has a group tablet check-in.

already_counted.description: Childcare worker confirms swap requests the system cannot decide and answers parents who still call.

incremental.description: Childcare worker corrects missed check-outs at the end of the day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small group with regular days and few swaps; high: a large flexible group with many swap requests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find activity ideas for the theme and age group, create developmentally appropriate lesson plans, discuss them with colleagues and prepare materials.

steps.what: Childcare worker looks for activity ideas for the theme and age group in books, websites and from colleagues

loop.input: The theme, the age band, an interest the worker logged for the group, and the centre's activity library tagged to its pedagogical plan.
loop.output: Three to five activity ideas, each naming a development goal from the centre's plan.
loop.check: Each idea must name a goal from the centre's plan and suit the age band in the library tags, or it is dropped; no child's name or health data goes into the step; the worker chooses and edits.
loop.stop: One set of ideas per theme week; the worker can ask once more with a new interest.
loop.why_not_simpler: The library holds known activities; a new interest needs a new idea.

steps.what: Childcare worker creates the developmentally appropriate lesson plans for the week in the template
Childcare worker discusses the plan with colleagues in the group
Childcare worker prepares the materials for the activities

tasks.design: The centre keeps an activity library tagged by age band and development goal in its childcare system ({OTHER}). A bounded step suggests a few activity ideas from the theme and a logged group interest, each naming a goal from the centre's plan, and the worker picks and edits them into a weekly plan template that pulls the chosen activities' goals and materials. Talking the plan over and preparing materials stay with the team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ideas were searched in books and websites each week and copied into a plan by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Early-years tools draft activity ideas from an area of learning or a child's interest.
tasks.still_hard: Fitting activities to this group on this day.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which activity will catch this group's attention.
tasks.altitude: Planning takes less searching; the team still decides.

reach.task: Keep the centre's pedagogical plan alive
reach.learn: Which goals the planned activities cover and which they miss.

evidence.claim: An early-years tool drafts activity ideas from an area of learning or a child's interest; educators check them.
In a trial, 129 school science teachers using a chat model with a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes (31%) with no quality difference seen (school teachers, not childcare).

assumptions: Boundary: from activity ideas to materials ready; carrying out activities is outside.
Input contract for s1: an activity library tagged by age and goal, kept by the pedagogical coach; group interests logged by the workers; fallback is searching.
The planning cut of about a third in s1 and s2 follows the teachers' trial; it is assumed, not measured, for childcare.
Talking with colleagues and preparing materials keep their full time.
unknowns: How much planning time workers have per week.
research_questions: How many suggested ideas are used?

already_counted.description: Childcare worker judges and edits suggested ideas for the group.

incremental.description: Childcare worker adds good activities to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an experienced worker repeating known themes; high: new themes and new staff who search a lot.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
